title: [Roadmap] Azure-first developer delivery across Control Plane and skills
body:
## First product outcome
Select a few real Azure Boards tasks from one project/repository, confirm they are ready, start one finite evening run, and return to inspectable local changes with current acceptance evidence, review results and the smallest remaining decisions. Deliver this through both ATL UI Control Plane and an installation of ATL skills alone.

This is the user-authorized planning scope dated 2026-11-04. It translates the two enhancement reviews into an executable sequence. It does not claim the runtime changes below have already shipped.

## Phase E0: preserve and finish the existing work
The baseline has 9 open issues and 1 completed issue; do not recreate them.

| Existing issue | Place in the execution order |
| --- | --- |
| #12 - CI for Plan/EGM suites | Completed; keep the closure and historical evidence. New changes still need current CI. |
| #4 - cross-process review/cost gate | Finish/verify the in-flight implementation first when using deep review. At planning time the issue remains open despite recent code commits. |
| #6 - parser/regression bank | Next deep-review correctness task; required before trusting that optional path. |
| #8 - staged progress/cancellation | Follow the correctness work. |
| #9 - browser deep-review journey | Exercise the completed UX and failure states. |
| #11 - plan finding disposition | Continue the existing policy phase; new code-task receipts reuse semantics without duplicating this work. |
| #10 - risk-based review depth | Add only after correctness and disposition are usable; keep optional policy scoped. |
| #5 - isolation probes | Explicit opt-in integration assurance; no automatic live calls. |
| #7 - backend benchmark | Bounded opt-in measurement after parser correctness; reuse results in P3. |
| #13 - working-tree ownership/commit waves | Coordinate scope throughout and before release; never sweep unrelated live manager state into commits. |

Suggested existing-work order: #4 -> #6 -> #8 -> #9 -> #11 -> #10 -> #5 -> #7; #13 ownership work runs alongside. This is a recommended queue, not a claim that every edge is a technical dependency. Optional deep-review improvements do not all block the Azure-first release. Keep deep review disabled/unclaimed until its applicable gates pass.

Baseline note: at commit 2468321316eaa83947556d3638170550b58c0314, runtime verification and docs deployment are green, but documentation verification failed (run 41793162185). Resolve the current failure in its owning work before the new release; do not reopen #12 merely to erase historical completion. The checkout contains unrelated local changes, so HEAD alone does not reproduce it.

## Phase P1: six small ordered delivery slices
- [ ] {{A1}} - common executable delivery contract and packaged portable helper.
- [ ] {{A2}} - readiness plus one reusable broken/fixed project verifier.
- [ ] {{A3}} - real Azure intake and a single-task local path in both surfaces.
- [ ] {{A4}} - actual file/behavior evidence and a current revision-bound delivery receipt.
- [ ] {{A5}} - finite unattended sequential batch, persisted limits and safe resume.
- [ ] {{A6}} - paired real pilot, install/quickstarts, current CI and release evidence.

Execute in that order. A single task becomes useful at {{A3}}/{{A4}}; unattended batch release is complete at {{A6}}. Start with concurrency 1 and two or three contained tasks. Reuse existing intake, workspaces, preflight, supervisor, recovery, diff and delivery gates. No new database, graph engine or always-on scheduling platform.

Each issue has separate Control Plane and skills-only scope, observable acceptance, impact paths, existing verification commands, explicitly proposed new tests and rollback. Do not close a dual-surface issue after implementing only the UI or only prose in a skill.

## Release acceptance
- [ ] One Azure project/repository/stack is declared; real source IDs/revisions trace through the receipts.
- [ ] A comparable small batch runs in isolated workspaces through both surfaces, with actual changed files, verifier/review evidence and explicit blockers.
- [ ] A controlled interruption and known repair are exercised; unresolved effects are reconciled instead of blindly replayed.
- [ ] Runtime and skills-only fixtures agree on completion/staleness/stop outcomes; the skills installation works without the manager service.
- [ ] Current acceptance evidence identifies final content including relevant dirty/untracked files; remaining blocking findings cannot be hidden by a successful worker exit.
- [ ] Usage coverage, failed attempts, manual interventions and review effort are reported honestly. Unknown usage is not zero.
- [ ] Relevant CI at the release revision passes, and each surface has a usable English quickstart.

Local delivery is distinct from a published PR, merge, deployment or Azure state update. Host availability, credentials, tool access and enforceable budget capabilities are explicit prerequisites. A skill cannot supply a scheduler or guarantee token enforcement by prompting alone. A tiny pilot cannot substantiate 99% reliability; first establish observable completion and bounded failure behavior.

## Follow-up phases, after the first release
- [ ] {{P2}} - operational memory, temporal provenance, recoverable writes and one tested preventer for a repeated failure.
- [ ] {{P3}} - accepted-outcome quality/cost, enforceable admission where possible, review capacity and held-out evaluation.
- [ ] {{P4}} - durable event bridge and optional routine/harness/knowledge adapters only where measured need exists.

These are future execution tracks, not hidden P1 requirements. Basic context selection, attempt capture and usage recording start in P1.

## Research-to-work coverage
| Enhancement | First delivery / follow-up |
| --- | --- |
| E01 reusable verifier | {{A2}}, real integration {{A3}}/{{A6}} |
| E02 structured task findings | Minimal {{A4}}, fuller history {{P2}}; existing #11 remains plan-specific |
| E03 provenance/receipt | {{A1}}/{{A4}} |
| E04 affected repair/invalidation | Basic {{A4}}/{{A5}}, richer closure {{P2}} |
| E05 correction to prevention | Capture {{A5}}, prove one preventer {{P2}} |
| E06 bounded bilingual retrieval | {{P2}} |
| E07 temporal knowledge/source independence | {{P2}} |
| E08 recoverable knowledge writes | {{P2}}, before concurrent knowledge writers |
| E09 event/executor | Finite Azure batch {{A3}}/{{A5}}, durable continuous bridge {{P4}} |
| E10 atomic tool budgets | Existing enforceable limits + coverage {{A5}}; stronger wrappers {{P3}} before wider concurrent paid dispatch |
| E11 progress/routine health | {{A2}}/{{A5}}, continuous routine health {{P4}} |
| E12 review capacity/outcome economics | Basic receipt/decision summary {{A4}}/{{A5}}, capacity/economics {{P3}} |
| E13 evaluation/ablation/routing | Cheap paired fixtures and real pilot {{A6}}, held-out comparisons {{P3}}; reuse #7 |
| E14 demonstrated routine promotion | Conditional {{P4}} |
| E15 harness adapter | Conditional {{P4}} |
| E16 readable projections/imports | Portable sourced knowledge {{P2}}, optional external projection {{P4}} |

- [X02: Gipp, event-driven workflow](https://x.com/gippp69/status/2115018135396905000)
- [X03: Bober, memory organization](https://x.com/Bober_smart/status/2078784709253841039)
- [X04: Plusxbt, repository collection](https://x.com/plusxbt/status/2117229536475496695)
- [X05: Shoopy, agent graphs and engineering](https://x.com/0xShoopy/status/2085383231554171098)
- [X06: Mr. Buzzoni, loop engineering](https://x.com/Mr_Buzzoni/status/2083061585858158636)
- [X07: Chase, development course](https://x.com/0xChaseTM/status/2109980695787454803)
- [X08: 0xwhrrari, harness engineering](https://x.com/0xwhrrari/status/2093685107534000560)
- [X09: 0xwhrrari, Grok Bot](https://x.com/0xwhrrari/status/2095497109524934750)
- [X10: Hanako, loops and graphs](https://x.com/hanakoxbt/status/2091515787366306154)
- [X11: Sergii, AI code reviewer survey](https://x.com/sermakarevich/status/2117599472188350701)
- [X12: Plusxbt, sourced and dated knowledge](https://x.com/plusxbt/status/2117565904951148756)

The local source catalog is research/briefs/2026-11-04-atl-enhancement-review.md (all twelve supplied X links and primary-source qualifications). The second batch and developer overnight roadmap remain background. The new first-delivery plan supersedes their ordering. Useful principles are carried into both surfaces; unverified marketing claims, inaccessible paid material and redundant frameworks are not product requirements.

## Next action
Start {{A1}} after checking the current issue/checkout ownership and the existing #4/#6 deep-review work. Do not begin by building advanced memory, purchasing a reviewer, running a large provider benchmark or adding another harness. Issue creation authorizes planning/publication only; each live run and remote side effect still needs the appropriate concrete authority.

title: [P1.1] Share a minimal task delivery contract across runtime and skills
body:
Tracking plan: {{A0}}.

## Outcome
A task has one small, versioned definition of ready, verified local delivery, blocked, and incomplete, understood by the Control Plane and a skills-only installation. This is executable glue for the next slices, not a replacement orchestration framework.

## Scope and existing foundation
Reuse the existing task lifecycle, role/evidence requirements, source snapshots and integration gates. Record source identity and revision, observable acceptance checks, allowed paths/actions, verifier identity, actual final content identity, check results, review disposition, unresolved decisions and usage coverage. Preserve the distinction between a Git commit and ATL content revisions, including admitted dirty and untracked content.

Start with a shared reference under skills/atl/references/developer-delivery.md and the smallest portable validation/receipt helper under skills/atl/scripts/ (new paths). Runtime imports or adapts that pure helper. Do not introduce a second database or a second authoritative lifecycle. If an existing pure utility already satisfies this contract, reuse it rather than extracting it unnecessarily.

## Control Plane
Adapt existing lifecycle/delivery boundaries to the common fields. Show the difference between verified local delivery, waiting for review, blocked and incomplete. Imported receipt JSON cannot grant authority or bypass role, verification or integration gates.

## Skills-only
Bundle the same reference/helper with ATL and route implement/verify/audit workflows to it. Run without a manager process or shared .trust/manager state. Record host capabilities, including execution, independent review, visual observation and budget enforcement. An instruction to stop spending is not an enforced quota.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A passing and a missing-evidence fixture produce equivalent normalized verdicts through runtime and portable entry points.
- [ ] Missing acceptance evidence, unresolved blocking findings or a changed final revision cannot yield verified delivery.
- [ ] A changed dirty/untracked source file invalidates the affected receipt; a Git SHA alone cannot conceal it.
- [ ] A forged pass field or imported receipt cannot advance an existing manager lifecycle gate.
- [ ] A skill install contains the helper and reference; it works in a temporary project without the Control Plane installed or running.
- [ ] Generated skill checks remain clean for the scoped edits, and existing task/role semantics remain compatible.

## Implementation map
Inspect runtime/lib/delivery.mjs, runtime/lib/handoffs.mjs and existing revision/evidence utilities before selecting an extraction boundary. Confirm the current callers and content-identity boundary. Touch canonical mode sources, skills/atl routing/references and packaging only as required. Callers at risk: integration, change review, installer and existing receipt readers. Avoid a migration in this slice; preserve compatibility with older stored records and mark unsupported receipt versions explicitly.

## Verification
Existing: python scripts/build_mode_skills.py --check; python verification/build_mode_skills_test.py; node verification/skill_install_test.mjs; node verification/queue_recovery_delivery_test.mjs.
Add: node verification/developer_delivery_contract_test.mjs with positive, stale, forged and skills-only packaging fixtures. A newly added assertion must fail on the corresponding broken behavior.

## Dependency and closure
Implementation entry point for {{A0}}. No hard dependency on optional deep review. Close only after both surfaces produce the same fixture verdicts and the linked evidence identifies the tested revision.

## Rollback and limits
Keep changes additive and restore existing readers if compatibility fails. Do not weaken existing gates to make receipt parity pass. Research coverage: E03; foundation for E01/E02/E04/E12/E13.

This work serves one Azure Boards project, one repository, one supported stack, and a finite set of preselected tasks. A locally verified delivery is distinct from a published PR or deployment. No unattended merge, deployment, new spending authority, or arbitrary backlog execution is implied.

Both surfaces must satisfy the same completion and evidence rules. Skills-only means the installed skills and their bundled portable helpers, without the Control Plane service or manager state. The host must provide the declared tools and permissions; missing capabilities produce an explicit limitation or blocker, never a passing claim.

Edit generated mode skills through skills/agent-trust-ladder/modes/*.md and regenerate using python scripts/build_mode_skills.py. Preserve unrelated work. New test filenames below are proposed implementation deliverables; their commands are not claims that these suites already exist or passed.

body:
Tracking plan: {{A0}}.

## Outcome
The developer starts one finite evening batch of ready Azure tasks, leaves it running, and returns to a terminal receipt for every selected task. Known safe failures receive bounded repair; an unresolved blocker cannot monopolize the whole night or masquerade as success.

body:
Tracking plan: {{A0}}.

## Outcome
